newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end weaker for seventh day in row.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end weaker for seventh day in row.

text.p: * But off the intra-day low of 3,173.92 pnts
Manila's share index finished lower for the seventh consecutive day but off its intra-day low on a rise in San Miguel Corp B shares, traders said.
"Investors generally don't want to take a strong position with the forthcoming long holiday. Foreign funds are definitely absent," said Poch Zamora, dealer at Peregrine Securities.
The main index closed at its support of 3,200.61, or 15.03 points lower.
The sharp drop in the main index was capped in late trade by index-linked San Miguel Corp B's recovery and Ayala Land Inc ending unchanged despite earlier losses.
All sectors fell with decliners edging out gainers 96 to 30 with 78 issues unchanged.
San Miguel B shares bucked the trend of the broad market by closing three pesos higher at 89.50 pesos.
Zamora said the issue was recovering from a selldown brought about by a foreign brokerage firm seeking to set up a package that allows foreigners to buy A shares of the food and beverage giant.
Market value turnover was lower than the daily average of three to four billion pesos. There were 8.10 billion shares traded valued at 2.218 billion pesos.

"The market continued to stay weak and it appears to be the absence of fresh incentives. The market is increasingly susceptible to a technical correction but reversals are unlikely yet," said Louie Bate, head of sales at ING Baring Securities.
Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital Equities, said the main index may test the support level of 2,900 on Thursday.
